text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: unusual external indexer ingestion detected — ~2k lines of staging-forwarder debug logs containing potential api_key fragments uploaded to external indexer (index.example.com). S3 path: s3://redwood-staging/forwarder/debug/2026-03-20/ (partial match)

oncall-eng: acked. linking logs now. any customer impact?

sec-ops: seeing sample lines with 'api_key=' and jwt fragments. looks like a debug-forwarder pushed unredacted traces to the indexer. potential creds in ~0.2% of lines.

carla: confirmed a few lines include staging service account token fragments. this is staging, but some customers have staging mirrors. tagging @mike-support to check customer exposure.

mike-support: checking list — two early-adopter customers enabled staging-log-mirror. opening bridge with them. pinging cust-success.

ben: can we stop the forwarder upload immediately? which job?

oncall-eng: disabling forwarder job now (job id: forwarder-staging-04). run: `kubectl scale deployment forwarder-staging --replicas=0 -n staging`

incident-bot: deploybot: deployment forwarder-staging scaled to 0 replicas by oncall-eng at 2026-03-20T16:12:05Z

sec-ops: good. next: rotate any staging service account keys and revoke tokens that match observed fragments. recommendation: immediate service-account key rotation + invalidate session tokens with matching prefixes.

sre-lead: oncall-eng, please run a targeted S3 scan to list all uploaded objects to indexer (we have indexer key in forwarder config). grep locally: ```
aws s3 ls s3://redwood-staging/forwarder/debug/2026-03-20/ --recursive | awk '{print $4}'
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-staging/forwarder/debug/2026-03-20/example.log - | grep -E "api_key=|Authorization: Bearer"
```

carla: i'm running the scan now. found 2,137 objects; sampling 200 shows ~4 with tokens. saving offsets for forensic.

sec-ops: initiating key rotation: creating new service-account key, updating staging deployments that need it after verification. also creating deny-list rules on indexer side — contacting indexer ops to request takedown of ingested data.

mike-support: customers notified via private thread; one customer confirmed they had no PII in their mirror but asked for timeline. preparing FYI.

legal: pls preserve logs/chain of custody. don't delete originals until instructed. we may need to notify depending on scope.

oncall-eng: rotating keys now. sequence: 1) create new key in KMS, 2) update forwarder creds in secret-manager, 3) deploy to any staging consumers, 4) revoke old key. I'll run steps and post statuses.

incident-bot: rotatortool: new key created (key-id: kg_9a7b). oncall-eng: proceed to secret update.

oncall-eng: secrets updated to use kg_9a7b, restarting dependent pods (rolling). will not revoke old key until verification completes.

carla: verified that indexer uploads stopped after scaling. indexer ops responded and began purge request; gave ETA ~90m for deletion from their index. they requested SHA list of objects — providing minimal list.

sec-ops: post-rotation actions: 1) revoke old key after confirming new key propagation, 2) run full grep across staging archive for further tokens, 3) begin scoped customer notification plan with legal & support, 4) open retro to fix debug masking in forwarder.

mike-support: customer bridge scheduled in 30m with affected customers. prepping transcript and mitigation summary.

legal: prelim assessment: low likelihood of regulated data exposure but must follow notification checklist if customer tokens were present. keep me in loop.

sre-lead: creating follow-up ticket to add masking at source and block public indexer endpoints in forwarder config. assigning to eng-runtime.

oncall-eng: handing off to sec-ops for continued mitigation and communications. I'm going offline for next shift. taking a short summary: forwarder scaled down, new key kg_9a7b active, indexer purge requested, customers notified.

sec-ops: taking it. will update last: we found zero production app keys; exposure limited to staging service-account fragments. continuing purge and full S3 grep. will post final scope once done. :white_check_mark:
